title: Persecution and Resistance Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll witness Nazi persecution of Jews and the few who dared resist.

concepts.def: Plan to murder all European Jews
Munich students led by the Scholls, 1942-43
Stauffenberg's failed bomb on Hitler, 20 July 1944

walkthroughs.body_html:
A boycott of Jewish shops on 1 April 1933 began legal persecution.

The Nuremberg Laws of 1935 stripped Jews of citizenship and banned marriage with 'Aryans'. By 1938 Jews could not own businesses or attend German schools.

On 9-10 November 1938 Nazis smashed 7,500 Jewish shops and burned synagogues on Kristallnacht.

30,000 Jewish men were sent to camps. After the 1942 Wannsee Conference the Final Solution began at Auschwitz, Treblinka and other death camps. About 6 million Jews were murdered.

Resistance was rare and risky. The Edelweiss Pirates brawled with Hitler Youth.

Hans and Sophie Scholl's White Rose handed out leaflets in Munich — they were beheaded in February 1943. On 20 July 1944 Colonel Stauffenberg's bomb at the Wolf's Lair failed to kill Hitler. 5,000 conspirators were executed.
